newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says to develop new oil fields.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says to develop new oil fields.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty co Ltd said on Friday it has received formal approval to proceeed with development of the Elang and Kakatua oilfields in Block 91-12 of the Australian-Indonesian Zone of Cooperation.
The cost of the project was estimated at A$94 million, A$40 million of which will be shouldered by BHP, the company said.
The oilfields, located about 525 kilometres from Darwin, would be developed using a leased floation, production, storage and offloading facility, with three subsea wells, BHP said.
Production of oil from the fields was expected to commence in the third quarter of 1998 and achieve an expected peak production rate of 33,000 barrels gross per day, BHP said.
Depletion of the field was expected to occur over two years, the company said.
BHP said it would act as operator of the fields on behalf of the partners.

Joint venturers in the Elang/Kakatua project are divisions of BHP (42.417 percent), Santos Ltd (21.426 percent) Inpex Sahul Ltd (21.209 percent), Petroz NL (13.371 percent) and Emet Pty Ltd 1.577 (percent).
The Skua Venture, a converted oil tanker, would be refurbished and leased for use the Elang and Kakatua project, BHP said.
The Skua field in the Timor Sea had produced about 20 million barrels of crude since first starting production in December 1991 but was now nearing the end of its economic life.
